Start: 15:00 PDT
Duration: 46 minutes
Attendees: Elena Martinez (Redwood AE), Samir Patel (Redwood SE), Jia Chen (Redwood CSM); Maya Thompson (Greenleaf Head of Platform), Amit Rao (Greenleaf SRE), Lina Gomez (Greenleaf PM), Tom Breen (Greenleaf Security)

Autoscale policy tuning: cooldowns, min/max, reserve buffer
Burst runbook and short-term dedicated bump
Security & KMS questions for Private deployment
Next steps and handoff to ops
transcript:
[00:00] Elena: hey everyone, thanks for joining, i think we have about 45 minutes, quick roll call?
[00:06] Maya: maya here.
[00:08] Amit: amit on the line.
[00:10] Lina: lina.
[00:12] Tom: tom, security.
[00:14] Samir: samir from redwood se.
[00:16] Jia: jia, csm.
[00:18] Elena: cool. quick agenda: one, run through last week's soak readouts; two, autoscale tuning suggestions; three, plan the burst run; four, security asks. sound good?
[00:29] Maya: yep, go ahead.
[00:31] Amit: just a heads up, logs are messy, some traces dropped at the tail end, oh and there's a weird p99 blip at minute 37 of the soak.
[00:40] Samir: yeah we saw that in the telemetry — p99 jumped from ~210ms to around 820ms for a two-minute window. looks correlated with simultaneous KV cache warm misses — or rather kv cash in the transcribed logs, sorry. could be prefix cache invalidation.
[00:57] Lina: do you think it's the model variant swap or something in our routing policy? we had two model variants pinned but fallbacks enabled.
[01:05] Samir: good question — our hypothesis: the routing fallback triggered to the quantized variant on a small subset, the runtime did a kernel recompile on that path. recompilation plus cold kv cache caused the spike. we have a mitigation: pre-warm the quantized variant and prepopulate the prefix cache for expected prefixes.
[01:28] Amit: ok, operationally, how do we pre-warm? we can't afford long warm processes during peak.
[01:34] Samir: two levers — proactive pre-warm job during off-peak and a small steady reserve of dedicated capacity (1-2 GPUs) to serve warm models so switchovers are fast. that's what the reserve buffer does.
[01:47] Elena: also tuning cooldowns on autoscale helps — if autoscale tears down too aggressively we lose caches. recommend min up-time 10 minutes and scale down cooldown 300s, scale up cooldown 30s in our template.
[02:00] Maya: those numbers sound high. can you justify 10 minutes? our cost team will push back.
[02:05] Samir: yes — it's a tradeoff. with a shorter tear-down you save money but pay with repeated warmup latency and p99 regressions. we ran a sim: with 5m cooldown p99 increases ~120ms averaged; with 10m it drops back under target. we'll share the sim csv.
[02:23] Lina: can you also show the cost delta? product wants to see dollars.
[02:27] Samir: absolutely, we'll include a delta column for tokens/sec cost and estimated infra spend for the pilot period.
[02:33] Jia: action item — samir to send policy + cost delta, elena to coordinate dedicated bump for burst test.
[02:40] Maya: about the burst test, we want it to mimic a real marketing surge: 3x baseline for two hours with spikes. can redwood provision that short term?
[02:50] Elena: yes, we can provision temporary dedicated capacity. billing will be pro-rated and we'll lock the bump just for the test window. will need formal request with window and expected concurrency.
[02:59] Amit: for the test we need to run it in a lower-risk window, preferably sunday 02:00-04:00 local, we'll dump traces to the shared folder. can you give us a checklist?
[03:09] Elena: we'll provide a runbook: pre-warm steps, traffic generator config, what telemetry to capture (p50/p95/p99, GPU mem, kernel stalls, kv cache hit rate), and where to upload logs.
[03:21] Tom: security questions — during the bump are logs still encrypted? what about KMS access and rotation? also we need to know if audit logs capture model versions and request IDs for compliance.
[03:33] Samir: logs remain encrypted in transit and at rest. for Dedicated and Private we support customer-managed KMS; rotation is supported but you need to schedule rewraps — we'll send the KMS guide. audit logs include model id, request id, route, and error codes. occasionally the transcription shows product names inconsistently — but the logs have canonical ids.
[03:52] Tom: great. we also need SOC2 scope confirmation — can you point to a docs link?
[03:57] Elena: yes i'll share our SOC2 summary and the SOC2 letter; samir will loop in security eng for any follow-ups.
[04:06] Amit: one operational hiccup from the soak: we saw a mismatch in token accounting between the app and the redwood usage report — about a 4% delta in tokens counted. any idea?
[04:16] Samir: sometimes the delta comes from streaming sessions being accounted differently and from retries. we found a bug in the client SDK where aborted streams didn't decrement a counter. we've got a patch we pushed to your test environment — can you confirm?
[04:28] Maya: confirmed we saw the patch, testing now. initial look suggests it's fixed but will run more test.
[04:33] Lina: on autoscale rules, we prefer rule-by-queue rather than global CPU because we have mixed workloads, is that supported?
[04:41] Samir: yes, we can do route-level autoscale with different thresholds (per-route p95 or queue length). for mixed workloads we recommend per-route min/max and a global emergency cap to prevent runaway costs.
[04:53] Maya: what's the emergency cap? and will it ever throttle legitimate spikes?
[04:57] Samir: it's a hard cap on total GPUs. if hit, policy can either reject new requests or fallback to a cheaper model variant. we usually set it to 150% of expected peak to avoid accidental throttle; fallback routes can be used for best-effort responses.
[05:12] Amit: fallback to cheaper variant worries us for correctness; our product needs high fidelity answers for certain flows. can we configure route-level fallbacks excluding critical routes?
[05:20] Samir: yes, route tags allow you to mark critical vs best-effort. critical routes will never fallback; they can be pinned to the primary variant and require reserve buffer planning.
[05:29] Tom: back to security — what about data residency during the bump? we need to ensure data stays in our EU region for EU traffic.
[05:36] Elena: we can pin region affinity and provision capacity in the requested region. need to confirm which region and the traffic split.
[05:42] Maya: EU traffic is about 22% of our baseline. ok, we'll include region split in the request.
[05:47] Samir: quick note about prefix caching — if you have long-tail prompts it's better to prepopulate cache with common prefixes. we can generate a suggested list from your logs.
[05:57] Lina: yes please. also, any notes on warm model memory with quantization — we've seen OOMs on the quantized variant during the test.
[06:04] Samir: quantized variants have lower memory but sometimes kernel fragmentation causes transient OOMs on specific hardware. mitigation: cap concurrency per model instance and set max batch size lower for quantized variant. we'll propose numbers.
[06:17] Amit: during the soak, we saw GPU mem climb and not reclaim fully until instance restart. is that expected?
[06:23] Samir: occasionally yes, on certain driver + kernel combos memory isn't fully returned until instance GC. we recommend scheduled rolling restarts during low windows in longer runs; for short bursts we keep reserve instances warm to avoid the effect.
[06:36] Maya: ok that's practical. next, the actual burst run—what telemetry will you need us to surface immediately during the run to make on-the-fly decisions?
[06:45] Elena: p99 latency per route, queue depth, GPU util, kv cache hit rate, and number of active model instances. also a simple health endpoint that returns model variant and instance id.
[06:57] Amit: we'll forward those metrics to our dashboard, but can you also provide a quick Slack alert playbook for critical thresholds?
[07:04] Jia: yes, i'll draft the Slack alert thresholds and escalation — sending examples this week.
[07:10] Samir: for thresholds, p99 > 1s for 2 consecutive mins, queue depth > 500, or GPU util > 95% for 3 mins should be triggers.
[07:20] Maya: ok we'll take those. one more ask: can we sanity-check billing for the bump? we need a pre-estimate.
[07:26] Elena: sure, we'll estimate based on extra GPUs * hours plus pro-rated infra. i'll include that in the autoscale policy doc.
[07:33] Tom: security follow-ups: what data flows into Redwood logs? do you redact PII by default?
[07:40] Samir: we don't redact automatically for PII; we recommend tokenization at the app layer or using redwood's field-level redaction SDK hooks. we'll send an integration guide.
[07:51] Amit: for the run we'll enable redaction hooks and mask user ids.
[07:55] Elena: excellent. to recap — samir sends autoscale policy + cost delta + pre-warm checklist; elena to provision bump and open billing ticket; amit runs burst and uploads traces; tom sends SOC2/KMS Qs; jia schedules handoff.
[08:12] Maya: sounds good. timeline?
[08:14] Elena: proposal — policy by Friday (8/21), temporary bump provisioned by Monday (8/24) for a test Wednesday night (8/26) — tentative, depends on your ops window.
[08:25] Lina: wednesday night might be tight, prefer sunday.
[08:28] Amit: sunday 02:00-04:00 works.
[08:31] Elena: ok sunday it is — we'll aim for 8/30 then.
[08:34] Jia: i'll put a calendar hold and send the runbook by Friday.
[08:38] Speaker 1: (background) cool.
[08:40] Elena: any final questions?
[08:42] Tom: none here.
[08:44] Maya: no, thanks.
[08:45] Elena: thanks everyone, we'll follow up in email with docs and next steps.
[08:49] (call ends)
